long_video.title: What Happens Inside a Data Center (Where the Internet Lives)
long_video.description:
Every photo, message and video you stream lives in a giant, windowless building full of computers. In this video we walk inside a data center: what happens when you tap play, what racks and servers are, how batteries and diesel generators keep the power on, why AI is pushing electricity use up so fast, and how hot aisles, cold aisles and liquid cooling fight the heat.

Chapters
00:00 Intro: where the internet lives
00:45 From your tap to a server
01:26 What's inside the building
02:08 Inside a rack
02:48 Power that never goes off
03:29 AI changed the power math
04:13 Hot aisles and cold aisles
04:57 When air isn't enough
05:38 Measuring efficiency: PUE
06:20 Built to never go down
06:59 Recap in three points
07:31 Your turn

Key facts (checked November 2026):
- Data centres used about 415 TWh in 2024, roughly 1.5% of global electricity; IEA projects about 945 TWh by 2030 (IEA Energy and AI, via Data Centre Magazine)
- Standard racks are 42U tall; 1U = 1.75 in (44.45 mm)
- Power path: grid, on-site substation, UPS batteries, diesel generators that start within seconds
- Nvidia H100 SXM: up to 700 W; an 8-GPU server draws around 10 kW
- Hot/cold aisle containment; liquid cooling with cold plates and immersion
- PUE: older sites around 2.0, industry average around 1.5, Google fleet around 1.1
- OVHcloud Strasbourg data center fire, March 2021

Sources
- IEA Energy and AI report (Data Centre Magazine summary): https://datacentremagazine.com/technology-and-ai/iea-asks-how-is-ai-reshaping-global-energy-demand
- IEA Energy and AI, executive summary: https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai/executive-summary
- Google data center efficiency: https://www.google.com/about/datacenters/efficiency/
- How datacenters actually work (DEV Community): https://dev.to/abhi1628/how-datacenters-actually-work-a-walk-through-the-building-nobody-sees-1mhm

Voiceover: AI-generated narration. Script researched and written for Tech Explained.
Music and stock footage: Mixkit (mixkit.co).
